rationale: BTrace is a smartphone tracing tool that manages trace buffers to retain longer continuous traces with low overhead. Its contribution is OS observability and buffer management, not compute kernels, fusion, numeric formats, or kernel generation.

The paper contributes the DaCapo Chopin Java benchmark suite and updated empirical methodologies for Java performance and garbage-collector analysis. These are benchmark/methodology contributions rather than kernel-level computation optimizations.

Cinnamon includes a Python DSL, polynomial/limb-level IRs, and compiler partitioning to expose program- and limb-level parallelism for encrypted ML inference. It is borderline because those compiler mechanisms are tied to a proposed scale-out FHE accelerator architecture rather than conventional kernels on existing hardware.

FEDORA is an ORAM-based federated-learning system for recommendation models with privacy/performance tradeoffs and SSD-friendly ORAM optimizations. The work is a privacy/storage/training system, not a new compute kernel or kernel compiler.

The paper addresses security use of ML-based dynamic predictions by adding statically computed invariants to distinguish mispredictions from attacks. Its mechanisms are program/security analysis above the compute-kernel layer.

CRUSH is a resource-sharing strategy inside dynamically scheduled HLS dataflow circuits for FPGAs, evaluated via RTL/HLS benchmarks. It improves hardware synthesis of circuits rather than providing software compute kernels, fusion, precision formats, or kernel-generation tooling of the kind counted here.

Necro-reaper is a software/hardware co-design using ISA hints, compiler support, and allocators to suppress dead memory traffic in warehouse-scale systems. This is memory-system optimization rather than a kernel-style compute optimization.

The paper proposes dynamic load shifting among microservice containers to exploit temporal/spatial imbalance in shared clusters. It is a cluster scheduling/resource-management system, not kernel-level computation.
Tela predicts temporal cloud-virtual-disk load characteristics and places disks to reduce overloads and imbalance. This is storage placement/resource management above kernels.
FleetIO manages multi-tenant cloud storage isolation/utilization using multi-agent reinforcement learning policies. Its contribution is storage-system control, not kernel-level compute optimization.
ZRAID changes how ZNS RAID uses the Zone Random Write Area to handle partial parity and reduce write amplification. It is a storage/RAID design rather than a compute-kernel optimization.
Marionette is a RowHammer attack exploiting coupled-row pairs in DRAM and analyzing bypasses of defenses. It is a security/memory vulnerability paper, not a kernel-style optimization.

HyperHammer is a RowHammer-based attack on KVM isolation using page steering and memory profiling. Its focus is virtualization/security exploitation, not compute kernels or kernel-generation techniques.

ReCA accelerates cooperative embodied agents through algorithm, system, and hardware co-design for planning, memory, communication, and execution. The contribution is an embodied-agent system architecture above the kernel layer, not a compute kernel or compiler for kernels.

AnA refactors an autonomous-driving stack so planning can guide perception through awareness/attention queries. It is an application/system design around perception scheduling, not a new DNN or GPU kernel.

SuperNoVA is an algorithm-hardware co-design for SLAM backends, including adaptive subtree selection and specialized hardware/runtime support. As an accelerator architecture for SLAM rather than a software compute kernel or kernel compiler, it is not kernel-style under the codebook.

The full text frames OctoCache as a software caching layer over OctoMap: it flattens voxel updates, orders cache evictions by Morton code, and overlaps octree updates on a CPU thread. These are data-structure/cache and application-system optimizations, not kernel-level compute scheduling/layout changes.

The paper introduces four new lossless floating-point compression/decompression algorithms and describes how their stages are implemented and parallelized on CPUs and GPUs. These are compute kernels for high-throughput scientific-data compression.

NACHO is a data-cache design for intermittently powered systems that integrates write-after-read detection to reduce checkpoint/runtime overheads. It is cache/memory-architecture support, not a compute-kernel optimization.

Fusion is an analytics object store that changes erasure-coded object layout and query-pushdown execution to reduce data movement. It is a storage/query-processing system rather than a kernel-style compute optimization.

Vela is a cloud-native virtualized infrastructure for large AI/LLM training, focusing on VM architecture, GPU Direct RoCE networking, storage, OpenShift operations, and cluster reliability. These are serving/training infrastructure mechanisms above the kernel-optimization layer.

The paper models AI-accelerator operator performance/power and inserts fine-grained DVFS SetFreq operations to save energy during model training. It schedules voltage/frequency around existing operators rather than contributing new kernels, fusion, precision formats, or kernel-generating compilers.
